observation_summary: The system throws ClassCastException when using RETURNS_DEEP_STUBS because it attempts to cast a generated mock object to an incompatible type (e.g., String, Number, Map.Entry).
reasoning_summary: The issue stems from the logic used to determine the return type of deep-stubbed methods. When the system encounters generic types or type variables, the algorithm for resolving the return type fails to correctly identify the expected class, leading to the creation of a mock that cannot be cast to the required return type. This is a procedural error in the type-resolution algorithm used by the deep stubbing mechanism.
evidence_used: java.lang.ClassCastException: class org.mockito.internal.creation.jmock.ClassImposterizer$ClassWithSuperclassToWorkAroundCglibBug$$EnhancerByMockitoWithCGLIB$$fdf68caf cannot be cast to class java.lang.String
java.lang.ClassCastException: class $java.lang.Comparable$$EnhancerByMockitoWithCGLIB$$1fc0096f cannot be cast to class java.lang.Cloneable
evidence_gaps: No production code snippets provided, only test failures and coverage summaries.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the failure manifests as a cast error, the root cause is the internal logic (algorithm) that resolves the generic type and decides what type of mock to return, rather than a mismatch in the interface contract itself.
The deep stubbing capability exists; the issue is a flaw in the logic used to resolve types within that capability, not a missing design-level feature.
